children.translated_text: In the morning, through bathing in the contemplation of <s>Śaṅkara</s> (Śiva), through sprinkling, through the restraint of the vital breaths (<s>prāṇāyāma</s>),

through the remembrance of <s>sandhyā</s> (twilight worship), purification (<s>mārjana</s>), removal of sin (<s>aghaśamana</s>), <s>upasthāna</s> (adoration), and <s>santarpaṇa</s> (offering of satisfaction),
through the worship of the door [of the shrine], approaching the abode of fire [i.e., the sacrificial hall], the removal of obstacles and other [rites] of the Lord —
he who, illustrious, performs the worship — for him alone is the twofold <s>siddhi</s> (attainment) [i.e., enjoyment and liberation].
In truth, the power (<s>śakti</s>) of the Lord (<s>Īśa</s>) is one, unlimited, taking many forms — she is <s>Śivā</s> (the auspicious Goddess).
Due to the condition of time (<s>kāla</s>), the twice-born (<s>dvijas</s>) daily [worship] her in the form of <s>Brāhmī</s> etc.,

children.text: dhyāyantyatra tu nirmalātmaśivayoḥ sandhiśca śaivī purā
children.translated_text: but here the junction (<s>sandhi</s>) of the pure Self and <s>Śiva</s> is the <s>Śaivī</s> [sandhyā] of old.

children.text: sandhyātaḥ śiva eva sādhakavarairdhyeyaḥ sadā nirmalaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>Śiva</s> alone, the pure one, should always be meditated upon by the foremost practitioners (<s>sādhakas</s>).
In the morning I remember [<s>Śiva</s>] who is established in the center of the heart-lotus,
whose nature is pure consciousness (<s>cit</s>), arisen transcending the paths of the moon and the sun,
who is always to be meditated upon by the best of sages for the attainment of liberation (<s>apavarga</s>),
the Lord (<s>Īśa</s>), the Self of the universe, the end of being and non-being, the infinite.
At midday, [I remember Him] who is radiant like a hundred thousand moons,
the Lord of the Universe (<s>Viśveśvara</s>), the Supreme Cause, immeasurable,
<s>Śambhu</s>, ever-arisen, whose nature is the illusion-free sky (<s>amāyaviyat</s>),
who resides in the middle of the bow [the eyebrow-center] — I constantly remember [Him].
At the beginning of night, [I remember] the imperishable <s>Brahman</s>, radiant like an ocean of nectar,
the Lord of the Universe, <s>Śiva</s>, established in the <s>nāda</s> (sound) arisen from the mantra,
the nectar of awakening (<s>bodhāmṛta</s>), devoid of instrument, cause, and effect,
Him who resides in the <s>brahmarandhra</s> (crown aperture) — I constantly remember.
At midnight, [I remember] <s>Śiva</s>, the immovable treasury of radiance,
who is to be known eternally by those who have turned away from sense objects, [who possess] the vision of the supreme truth,
the imperishable, the inconceivable, beyond conceptualization,
whose domain transcends <s>unmanī</s> (the state beyond mind) — I constantly remember.
Contemplating the Self-nature — the pure, luminous state of <s>Sadāśiva</s> pervading to the end of the <s>Śuddhavidyā</s> (Pure Knowledge) <s>tattva</s>,
[which is attained by] one whose feet are placed in the sequential order of <s>tattvas</s> from the Earth-knot to the end,
performing all the excellent rites following the supreme method established through <s>Śaiva</s> knowledge —
[one should] make the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) [abide] in the heart itself, stationed within [the powers of] sun, moon, fire, space, and <s>śakti</s>.

children.text: āyāmaiḥ śvanasya bhautikamalaṃ dehaṃ kalābhiḥ sudhīr
children.translated_text: The wise one who, through extensions (<s>āyāmas</s>) of the breath, purifies the material-impurity-laden body by means of the <s>kalās</s> (phases)
that extend through the five paths (<s>pañcādhvan</s>), constantly purifying with their mantric armors (<s>chambaras</s>),
[who,] bearing a body adorned with mantras, satisfies [<s>Śiva</s>] by night and day at the <s>sandhyās</s> (junction times)
through worship (<s>arcā</s>), oblation (<s>homa</s>), and <s>samādhi</s> — that one attains the <s>Śaiva</s> state of <s>Śiva</s>.
He who is this God, greater than the great,
subtler than the subtle — by those who fear [the cycle of] existence,
He is to be known as <s>Śiva</s>, all-pervading, within the body;
He is to be meditated upon and worshipped in the midst of the <s>Śivaliṅga</s>.
In the <s>Śiva</s>-temple called the heart-lotus, upon the <s>Mind-born</s> [Kāma] seat,

children.text: tatkarṇikākhye kriyāpīṭhe jñānamayaṃ viśuddhamanasā saṃsthāpya nādātmanā
children.translated_text: upon the action-pedestal (<s>kriyāpīṭha</s>) called its pericarp, having established with a pure mind, through the nature of <s>nāda</s> (sound), the <s>liṅga</s> made of knowledge (<s>jñānamaya</s>),

children.text: liṅgaṃ tacca sudhāmayena payasā saṃsnāpya samyakpuno
children.translated_text: and having bathed that [<s>liṅga</s>] well with the nectar-water of <s>sudhā</s> (ambrosia), and then again
with the sandalwood paste of dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>), and with the flowers of <s>ahiṃsā</s> (non-violence) etc. as offerings (<s>vasus</s>),
with incense (<s>dhūpa</s>) [in the form of] <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath-control), with the offering of the lamp of consciousness (<s>ciddīpa</s>),
with the food-offering of the <s>soma</s> (nectar) [in the form of] sense-withdrawal (<s>pratyāhāra</s>), and with <s>japa</s> (repetition) [along] the <s>suṣumnā</s>,
and with ornaments born of pure meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>) through manifold concentrations (<s>dhāraṇās</s>) upon that [<s>liṅga</s>] in the mind,
with the offering of identity (<s>sāmyā-nivedana</s>) — he who worships thus is blessed and pure indeed!
Having gratified the fire (<s>anala</s>) in the sacrificial pit (<s>kuṇḍa</s>) located at the navel, with the offering of nectar flowing from the moon,
when [the Lord], pervading all, abides in the sky (<s>vyoman</s>) that is the abode of <s>Śiva</s>, the nature of <s>Īśa</s>,
through the flame of the subtle <s>Śiva</s>-sound (<s>Śivāṇu-nāda</s>) arising from the <s>kanda</s> (bulb), through the self-awareness of the [mental] activity —

children.text: śaive jyotiṣi yaḥ karoti puruṣo muktaḥ sa evākṣayaḥ
children.translated_text: the person who effects [this] in the <s>Śaiva</s> light — that one alone is liberated, imperishable!
When the self-supporting substance-mantras,
the self-dependent <s>liṅga</s> and other [ritual objects] have been properly purified,
for practitioners established on the path of <s>Siddhānta</s>,
may Your worship not be performed in reverse order!
The seed (<s>bīja</s>) of the <s>śakti</s> called <s>dhārikā</s>, the bud of the infinite lotus,
the four [petals] in reverse [order] — the stations of merit (<s>puṇya</s>), awakening (<s>bodha</s>), dispassion (<s>virāga</s>), and sovereignty (<s>bhūti</s>),
the body [of the seat], the two coverings, the lotus with its filaments and pericarp,
endowed with the assemblage of the circles of <s>śakti</s> — I bow to the seat of <s>Śiva</s> (<s>Śivāsana</s>)!
The bulb (<s>kanda</s>) of earth, the stalk [extending] up to the end of the <s>Kāla</s> (Time) <s>tattva</s>,
the mass of worlds as its thorns, the thread of existence (<s>bhāvasūtra</s>),
the knot at each node, the lotus of <s>Śuddhavidyā</s> (Pure Knowledge),
with its eight petals upon which <s>Vidyeśāna</s> [and other lords] are mounted,
rich with the filaments and pericarp [representing] the <s>śaktis</s> beginning with <s>Vāmā</s>,
together with the orbs of the sun etc. — the excellent <s>yogapīṭha</s> (seat of yoga) —
the Self-mantra situated within the heart-mantra, established there,
and the Lord (<s>Īśa</s>) who has entered the <s>bindu</s> (point) — I bow to His form!

children.text: tatkandaṃ śatakoṭiyojanamitaṃ nālaṃ parārdhāntakaṃ granthiḥ koṭiparārdhapaścimasahasro 'bjaṃ ca tallakṣakam /
children.translated_text: Its bulb measures a hundred koṭi yojanas; the stalk extends to the end of a parārdha; the knot is one thousand [units] after a koṭi-parārdha; and the lotus is one hundred thousand [units].

children.text: mūrtistasya ca koṭirīśvaramayī tasyārbudasyārbudāmbhojaṃ mantramayaṃ sadāśivavapustadvānameyaḥ śivaḥ //
children.translated_text: His form is a koṭi, of the nature of <s>Īśvara</s>; its arbuda of arbudas is the mantra-lotus — the body of <s>Sadāśiva</s>; beyond that, immeasurable, is <s>Śiva</s>. //
Whose supreme form at the <s>bindu</s> consists of herbs, ornament, and sound,
to be meditated upon by those devoted to the mantra and <s>tantra</s> of <s>Śaṅkara</s> — <s>Śivā</s> (the Goddess), whose limbs are knowledge and action,
bestower of all sovereignty and bliss, incomparable, of the nature of <s>Sadāśiva</s>, pure —

children.text: nādākhyāya sadāśivāya mahate śāntāya tasmai namaḥ
children.translated_text: to that great <s>Sadāśiva</s>, called <s>Nāda</s> (Sound), the peaceful — to Him, homage!
He is always to be meditated upon, abiding in the center of the sphere of the sky (<s>gaganamaṇḍala</s>),
stationed in the heart-lotus of the <s>Śiva</s>-yogin who is free from obstacles and pure,
whose body is the partless (<s>niṣkala</s>) <s>Śiva</s> beyond <s>Īśa</s>, together with <s>Sadāśiva</s> —
the <s>Bindu</s> (Point), containing the Lords of the Worlds born of the <s>kalās</s> (phases) that arise from <s>svara</s> (vowel-sound).
He whose <s>Īśāna</s> [face] is the crown, whose <s>Nara</s> face is the lotus [of the face], whose heart is <s>Aghora</s>, whose secret [parts] are <s>Vāma</s>,
whose body is <s>Sadyojāta</s>, whose stations are <s>Pura</s> (body), <s>Īśāna</s>, <s>Ana</s> (breath), and <s>Hṛdaya</s> (heart), whose nature is the six-fold path (<s>ṣaḍadhvan</s>),
whose body is composed of elements (<s>bhūta</s>), ocean, <s>siddhi</s>, <s>Smara</s> (Kāma), serpent, and <s>kalā</s> — [having the form of] action (<s>kriyā</s>), will (<s>icchā</s>),
and vision (<s>dṛk</s>), with a month and a half as His three eyes — I praise Him, situated in the <s>kalā</s>s, whose body is <s>Vidyā</s> (Knowledge).
With the colors of the <s>Brahma</s>-limbs: white, red, black, yellow, crystal, moonlike, golden, crimson, and fire-colored,
His manifest form, through union with <s>Bhavahara</s> (Destroyer of Existence) <s>Śiva</s>, appears crystal-like.
Due to the oneness of mantra and meaning — thus in all <s>Śaiva</s> doctrines — this is called the cause of all purposes.
The difference of colors among the faces is the wondrous essential nature of the Lord of the conscious and the unconscious.
By <s>Īśāna</s>, which is sky-natured and of white radiance, the supreme Lord's
four faces — of the nature of the mantras <s>Puruṣa</s>, <s>Hṛdaya</s>, <s>Guhya</s>, and <s>Aja</s> — are pervaded.
Therefore, the knowers of <s>Śiva</s> [say] this is of white radiance. [But] those who dwell in the eastern and other directions,
due to the grace directed at [particular] colors, know each face as having yellow and other colors.
<s>Śiva</s> whose faces are <s>Īśāna</s>, <s>Tatpuruṣa</s>, <s>Aghora</s>,
<s>Vāma</s>, and <s>Aja</s> (Sadyojāta) —
having the forms of child, youth, elder, woman,
and man — I bow to Him.
The Lord (<s>Īśa</s>) who bears the trident (<s>triśūla</s>) and the skull-staff (<s>khaṭvāṅga</s>), [accompanied] by His <s>Śakti</s>,
with the boon-granting [hand] and lotus [hand], and the gesture of fearlessness (<s>abhaya</s>),
attached to the blue lotus, the serpent, and the <s>ḍamaru</s> (drum),
with the <s>bījapūra</s> (citron fruit), the beautiful one, holder of the rosary (<s>akṣasūtra</s>) —
The three powers (<s>śaktis</s>) of the Lord (<s>Vibhu</s>), consisting of awakening and bliss, which destroy the fear of [worldly] existence,
and through transformation [they are] the unfolding of the seed of all things:
the complete [<s>kalā</s>] is <s>Prakṛti</s>, that which faces the <s>kalā</s> etc. is the long rosary, [and] the mind (<s>manas</s>) —
the collection of weapons of <s>Śambhu</s> should be known by those versed in the <s>Āgamas</s> as the supreme, not the inferior.
To <s>Īśāna</s>, the lord of all <s>vidyās</s> (sciences), the Lord of beings,
the overlord of <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Sadāśiva</s> of partless (<s>niṣkala</s>) form, [born] of <s>Brahman</s>-nature — I praise Him! //
To <s>Tatpuruṣa</s>, the great god (<s>Mahādeva</s>) who bestows <s>Śaiva</s> knowledge upon devotees,
<s>Rudra</s>, the impeller of the <s>tattvas</s> (principles) for the attainment of the state of <s>Śiva</s> — I venerate Him! //
Now, <s>Aghora</s>, the non-terrible, who removes the noose of the bound soul (<s>paśupāśa</s>), the most terrible of the terrible,

children.text: this half-line appears to be unmetrical āryā

children.translated_text: the refuge from all [dangers] — I venerate <s>Śarva</s>, the many-formed! //

children.text: vāmaṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ raudraṃ kalavikaraṇaṃ balavikaraṇaṃ kāntam /
children.translated_text: <s>Vāma</s>, <s>Jyeṣṭha</s>, <s>Raudra</s>, effecting transformation of <s>kalā</s>, effecting transformation of power, beautiful (<s>Kānta</s>),
crushing of power, subduing of all beings, and the mind-transcending (<s>Manonmana</s>) — I venerate [Him]! //
<s>Sadyojāta</s>, the omniscient, who removes the fear of existence (<s>bhavabhaya</s>) for those who bow,

children.text: this half-line appears to be unmetrical āryā

children.translated_text: the supreme unifier of existence, the pure one, born of existence (<s>Bhavodbhava</s>) — I praise the Lord of the world! //

children.text: this half-line appears to be unmetrical āryā

children.translated_text: Through the flame of the <s>nāda</s> (sound) arising from the glorious root mantra, [ascending through] the stations of <s>Brahmā</s>, etc., up to <s>Sadāśiva</s>,
by the sequential departure and passage, resplendently upward, established within the sky at the end —
to You, consisting of awakening and bliss, the Lord of all, eternal, the Self of the Universe,

children.text: śuddhāyāmalatejase ca mahate tasmai parasmai namaḥ
children.translated_text: to the pure one, of immaculate splendor, the great one — to that Supreme One, homage!
Moon-pair, quality, object, measure, its half, its portion, sixteen,
two-more-than-thirty, ocean, sixty, serpent, hearing, and earth,
vision, arrow-hand, part, reality — thus [enumerated] is <s>Unmanī</s>, the supreme seat (<s>paramāsana</s>)

children.text: yasya taṃ praṇato 'smi niṣkalamavyayaṃ paramaṃ śivam
children.translated_text: of Him — to that partless (<s>niṣkala</s>), imperishable, supreme <s>Śiva</s> I bow!
The first, the fifth, death, ornament, half-moon, quality, eye, vision,
sun, sound, sickle, radiance, moon, circle, plough-form,
with rays, three-pointed, two-orbed, two-curved, serpent — <s>Unmanī</s>:

children.text: pātu vaḥ sakalāparaḥ sakalākalaḥ sakalaḥ śivaḥ
children.translated_text: may <s>Śiva</s>, who is all-with-parts (<s>sakala</s>), beyond all-with-parts (<s>sakalāpara</s>), all-with-parts-and-without-parts (<s>sakalākala</s>), and pure-all (<s>sakala</s>), protect you!
The partless (<s>niṣkala</s>) [<s>Śiva</s>], adorned with <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, individual soul (<s>pudgala</s>), ornament, and half-moon,
with dam, staff, its end, and the four <s>śaktis</s>, [and] the <s>Īśvara</s>-Yogin,
<s>Śaṅkara</s>, who moves with eight-ocean-fingers [i.e., a specific measure], who goes to the essence-void (<s>rasaśūnya</s>),
the Lord of all mantras, the palace (<s>prāsāda</s>) [mantra] — I bow to the one who traverses the six paths (<s>ṣaḍadhvan</s>)!
Through the manifestation, establishment, seeing, and restraint of consciousness — with the superior <s>mudrās</s>, with the unity of limb-[mantras] and <s>Śiva</s>,
through foot-washing (<s>pādācama</s>), oblation-water (<s>arghya</s>), generation, and offerings — Your worship, O <s>Maheśa</s>, is the fruit of [this] birth! //

children.text: āvāhanaṃ svātmani citprakāśas tatra sthitiḥ sthāpanamīśvarasya /
children.translated_text: Invocation (<s>āvāhana</s>) is the radiance of consciousness within one's own Self; establishment (<s>sthāpana</s>) therein is the establishment of the Lord;
proximity (<s>sānnidhya</s>) is the presence of the Self and the Lord together; confinement (<s>saṃrodhana</s>) is the restraint of one's own [self] in <s>Śiva</s>. //
Homage to <s>Bhava</s> (Śiva), whose heart is consciousness and bliss! Homage to Him whose form is distinguished by qualities and sovereignty!
Homage to the crest (<s>śikhā</s>) [which is] self-dependent power! Homage to Him whose nature is the radiance-armor (<s>tejaḥkavaca</s>)! //
Homage to the one who bears the trident (<s>śūlin</s>), who wields the weapon of blazing power against the impurities of the bound souls (<s>paśus</s>) that they cannot endure;
Homage to the Unchanging One (<s>avikāra</s>), whose form is the six limbs (<s>ṣaḍaṅga</s>), to <s>Sadāśiva</s> (the Eternally Auspicious), whose form is immortality (<s>amṛta</s>) — homage!
To <s>Śiva</s>, who is pure by nature — the water for sipping (<s>ācamana</s>) [offered] at his feet is for the purpose of one's own purification;
the offering of <s>arghya</s> (oblation water) and the presenting of flowers — this is for the attainment of his auspicious abode.
The bathing (<s>snāna</s>) removes one's own impurity; the anointing with auspicious fragrances,
the fine garments and ornaments, the worship with fragrant flowers and garlands,
the offering of incense according to the rules to <s>Sadāśiva</s> adorned with ornaments, [which is] for your [benefit] —

children.text: bhogārthaṃ hi sadeśadhāmni vimalaṃ dīpaṃ śivajñānadam
children.translated_text: for the purpose of enjoyment (<s>bhoga</s>) in his auspicious abode, [one offers] the stainless lamp that bestows the knowledge of <s>Śiva</s>.
Situated in [the positions of] <s>Īśa</s> (the Lord), <s>Rakta</s> (the Red), <s>Pāni</s> (Wind), <s>Indra</s>, <s>Mṛtyu</s> (Death), <s>Ke</s>, and <s>Indu</s> (Moon),
with faces resembling clouds, the sun, wind, and fire,
with hands holding [attributes including] the boon-granting and fear-dispelling [gestures], the trident (<s>triśūla</s>), and the spear (<s>śakti</s>), in pairs of faces,
homage to those born from the limbs of <s>Śiva</s>, whose forms are the <s>mantras</s> beginning with <s>Hṛdaya</s> (Heart).
The worship of the subsidiary limbs (<s>bhogāṅga</s>) is for the purpose of attaining the qualities of <s>Śiva</s> — [namely] unity with the Lord;
and again, the worship of the limbs is for the union with <s>Śiva</s> of the worshipper of purified self;
the offering of food (<s>annanivedana</s>), water, mouth-fragrance, and other gifts to one who is [already] satisfied [signifies] that the mind
[should be directed] toward contentment — [this is] the wondrous, auspicious, and meritorious fruit of worship therein.
The giving of the sacred thread (<s>pavitra</s>) to one who is [already] purified
[serves as] the destroyer of the threefold suffering (<s>tāpatraya</s>), for the accomplishment of all aims;
and <s>japa</s> (repetition) with devotion, and prostration to <s>Śiva</s>,
is the cause for [attaining] the status of <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and the other [gods].
In [external] worship, [<s>Śiva</s> is understood as] <s>sakala</s> (with parts); in <s>japa</s>, as <s>sakala-akala</s> (both with and without parts), [and as] eternally arisen;
as <s>niṣkala</s> (without parts, transcendent), pervading all paths (<s>sakalādhvaga</s>), and complete in the offering of the self (<s>ātmasamarpaṇa</s>);
as <s>Hara</s> (the Destroyer) in the sky [of consciousness], brilliant like crystal, in the [ritual] domain endowed with <s>kalā</s> (phases) —

children.text: yo hi vetti paraṃ śivaṃ śiva eva so 'stra na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: whoever thus knows the supreme <s>Śiva</s>, he is <s>Śiva</s> himself — there is no doubt in this.
The repeated worship (<s>bhūyaḥ pūjana</s>) brings about the proximity of the Lord; the supplication (<s>samprārthana</s>) is for
the mutual beholding of the Lord and the self in this world, and for enjoyment (<s>bhoga</s>) in the realm of <s>Sadāśiva</s>;
the worship of the Lord's fire (<s>īśāgnyarcana</s>) and the offering (<s>arpaṇa</s>) are for the destruction of the threefold bondage of <s>karma</s>;
the self-offering (<s>svātmanivedana</s>) to the Supreme <s>Śiva</s> should be known as being for the establishment of the self [in <s>Śiva</s>].
For the purpose of the external ritual (<s>bahiṣkriyā</s>) [that removes] the mass of impure <s>tattvas</s> (principles),
the <s>arghya</s> (oblation) is [offered] facing away, to <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord);
one who makes the emission (<s>visarga</s>) that causes establishment in that [state]
attains the state of <s>Śiva</s> (<s>śaivaṃ padam</s>).
<s>Jñānaśambhu</s>, a distinguished <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, a native of the <s>Cola</s> country, a learned one (<s>sūri</s>),
composed this pure hymn of worship to <s>Śambhu</s> (<s>Śiva</s>);
a knower of <s>Siddhānta</s>, by the word of <s>Śiva</s>,
he composed [it] with devotion, for [both] enjoyment (<s>bhukti</s>) and liberation (<s>mukti</s>).
